newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Luxury Indonesian shopping complex a charred wreck.
newsitem.headline: Luxury Indonesian shopping complex a charred wreck.

text.p: Banjarmasin's Mitra Plaza was a glitzy four-storeyed shopping and cinema complex at the heart of the commercial centre in this city on Indonesia's half of Borneo island.

On Sunday, it was a charred wreck and nervous soldiers had blocked off the shell of the building while rescue workers said they had brought out at least 130 bodies from within what had once been a luxury glass-fronted edifice.

Clashes between rival political groups on the last day of campaigning for May 29 general elections on Friday quickly deteriorated into widespread rioting in Banjarmasin after residents said police were slow to clamp down.

Looters thronged the Mitra Plaza, but remained inside, first because police had made a belated entry to the scene and later when they were trapped by flames from a bank ransacked and set ablaze on the ground floor, witnesses said.
By early afternoon on Sunday, authorities had located 130 bodies at the site, quietly taking the corpses away in ambulances from behind the building out of sight of journalists and photographers.
"There will be many more," one official said.
At least four others died in rioting elsewhere in the city.
"All of them (at the Mitra) were criminals. They were taking advantage of the riots. There were no employees among them," one rescue official at the scene told Reuters.
Police said most of the 181 people arrested were looters.
Officials say the Mitra Plaza was the last target for a wild mob before security forces re-took control of the city centre late on Friday night.
Fearing violence, most shops, including those on the four-level Mitra Plaza had closed early in the afternoon and sent their employees home.
On Sunday, advertisements outside the cinema complex still enticed viewers to see Chinese or Hollywood action films. But there were no queues of movie-goers.
Instead, young soldiers in camouflage greens complained of getting no sleep in three days as they twirled their M-16 rifles while calling to a foreign photographer not to take pictures.

A Reuters reporter and photographer were allowed to visit the scene for only about 10 minutes under escort by a uniformed police officer and an information department official after receiving clearance from military intelligence in the national capital Jakarta, 885 km (550 miles) to the southwest.
"Those who died were mostly trapped on the second floor as they ran up there to hide after security forces starting patrolling the streets," one rescue official said.
Most residents in Banjarmasin, described by guidebooks as the Venice of Indonesia for its river canals and floating markets, said they stayed inside on Friday night.
"Even the ambulance drivers refused to go out. They feared they would be hurt," one doctor at the Ulin general hospital said. "Fire engines were attacked and stoned," said another witness.

On the streets anarchy temporarily ruled as locally-based police and troops waited for reinforcments to be flown in from neighbouring provinces and the main island of Java, 90 minutes flying time away.
As the authorities waited for help, the trail of destruction spread.
It started with the torching of the provincial headquarters of the ruling Golkar party after clashes between Golkar loyalists and those from the rival Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP).

Then rioters set ablaze a Protestant Batak minority church which in turn ignited a crowded neighbourhood of wooden houses, destroying hundreds of homes which were still smoking 48 hours after the event.
The mob later trashed a branch of the Lippo Bank, a supermarket and a shopping mall under the four-star Hotel Kalimantan, later setting all ablaze in what was to become a pattern.
"They looted first before they burnt the shops," one policeman said. "It has not yet been calculated how much was lost, but they took all the money from the Lippo Bank," he added.
"The violence was extraordinary," one priest said.
